participants: Andrew Jin / Andrew Musial (closer, Primal Instinct)
summary: Manager one-to-one focused on objection handling. Chris tells Andrew his month-to-date call-to-close rate is 33.3% against a 25% KPI and that his two fixable weaknesses are the pitch and end-of-call objection handling - specifically, attacking every small objection instead of isolating whether it is the real one, and cutting prospects off mid-disclosure. He walks through how to distinguish a genuine finances objection from fear using the double tie-down, and lays out how he sizes payment plans against a prospect's monthly surplus so they are not left with nothing. Andrew asks when to present the three-month downsell and whether 'love it or leave it' is the right fallback; Chris says no, the answer is to walk them through the fear. They also cover CRM disposition rules (lost versus follow-up) and the double-booking policy, prompted by a prospect who withdrew after being over-messaged and then called ten minutes late.
notable: Stated pricing structure beyond the published offer: a three-month tier exists as a downsell for prospects who can only afford three months, and third-party financing on the $6,000 programme is quoted internally as $7,200.

Payment-plan policy stated explicitly: size the instalment against disclosed monthly surplus, roughly 65% of it, and do not take a prospect down to nothing - 'we never want to put anybody in a spot where they have to sell their couch'. Chris also says he only proposes something aggressive 'if they suggest it'.

Double-booking is confirmed as deliberate company policy because of historic show rates: two prospects are booked into every closer slot and the overflow is handed to another closer or re-triaged by a setter.

A prospect withdrew that week because of the double-booking: over-messaged with confirmations then called ten minutes past the hour. Chris's prescribed response is an apology that leaves the door open.
CRM disposition rule stated: 'lost' is only for an explicit no or a competitor purchase; everything else is 'follow-up'. This directly shapes what a close-rate denominator looks like.

Chris's stated position on when to downsell to three months: only 'if you find out they only have enough money to do the three-month option' - which is not how the three-month tier was used on the 2026-06-15 EJ Hernandez call.
